sections.content: A key use of the imperfecto is describing what something or someone WAS LIKE in the past — their appearance, character, emotional state, or situation. These are background states, not completed events.

items.spanish: La casa era grande y tenía un jardín bonito.
items.english: The house was big and had a pretty garden.
It was very cold and it was raining.

items.spanish: Me sentía muy cansado después del trabajo.
items.english: I felt very tired after work.

items.spanish: Había mucha gente en el mercado.
items.english: There were a lot of people at the market.
She seemed young but she was 50.

sections.content: 'Había' is the imperfecto of 'haber' and means 'there was' or 'there were' — it is always singular in Spanish: había un gato / había tres gatos.
Common imperfecto state verbs: ser (era), estar (estaba), tener (tenía), haber (había), querer (quería), poder (podía), saber (sabía), parecer (parecía), sentirse (me sentía).
